audit_title: QuantEngine Phase 175 Forensic Findings — Contract Multiplier, Notional & Fee-Basis

findings.title: Forensic Resolution of the $42,082 vs $82 Notional Basis Discrepancy
findings.description: Independently audited the reported canonical entry price. Proved that the published round-trip maker fee of $0.03871580 USD mathematically requires an entry price of $82,000.00 USD (yielding a fee-bearing notional of $82.00000 USD at 0.001 multiplier). Proved that an entry price of $42,082.00 USD yields an entry notional of $42.08200 USD and round-trip maker fees of $0.01987450 USD. Confirmed that all executable code and JSON artifacts strictly use $82,000.00 USD, and that '$42,082.00' was an accidental transcription typo in the narrative table header of the Phase 174 summary for the contemporaneous Level-2 order book ask price ($82,082.50 USD).

findings.title: Authoritative Delta Exchange India BTCUSD Contract Specifications
findings.description: Verified from data/fixtures/delta/delta_mcp_public_products_20260925.json that BTCUSD (Product ID 84) is a vanilla linear perpetual futures contract (notional_type: 'vanilla', is_quanto: false) with contract_value = 0.001 BTC, settled and quoted in USD. One contract represents 0.001 BTC. P&L is linear: (exit - entry) * multiplier * quantity.

findings.title: Exact Single-Application of Multiplier, Quantity, and Notional
findings.description: Verified that contract multiplier (0.001) and quantity are applied exactly once during notional construction in core/execution/maker_execution_model.py (leg1_notional = ep * cm * qty). Fees are evaluated strictly on single-leg notionals with zero double-counting or unit inconsistencies.

findings.title: Deterministic Tax and Monetary Precision Stability
findings.description: Verified that Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST) of 18% is applied strictly to broker commissions using Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP quantization to 8 decimal places. Rebate tiers pay zero GST. Effective maker rate is 2.36 bps; effective taker rate is 5.90 bps.

findings.title: Friction Hurdle Gate Rule Hierarchy & Subsumption Proof
findings.description: Formally proved that Rule 1 (fee-to-target ratio <= 40%) strictly subsumes Rule 2 (target multiple >= 2.0x breakeven) under codebase definitions, because Target Multiple = 1 / Fee Ratio, and 1 / 0.40 = 2.50x >= 2.00x. Rule 2 is retained for backwards compatibility and serialized diagnostics. Rule 3 (post-fee R:R >= 1.25) is an independent binding constraint depending on stop loss distance.

findings.title: Fail-Closed Boundary Hardening & Zero Live Adapter Invocation
findings.description: Verified that evaluate_friction_hurdle fails closed safely on None, NaN, Inf, negative prices, zero quantities, and zero target distances. Verified that rejected signals halt order dispatch immediately, and assert_no_live_adapter_invocation() passes across all test executions.

findings.title: Temporal Non-Overlap of Available Candle and L2 Datasets
findings.description: Audited data lineage and proved that 1m.parquet (1,440 continuous rows from September 5, 2026) and delta_ob_updates_archive.json (113 L2 frames from October 19, 2026) are temporally disjoint windows with zero overlap. Synchronized signal-to-execution claims remain prohibited.

findings.title: Strict Scope of Unprofitability & Expectancy Classifications
findings.description: Distinguished between a strategy failing a specific modeled cost scenario versus being universally unprofitable. Proved that while 4.5-pt, 15-pt, and 50-pt setups fail under 2.36 bps maker fees, this does not imply universal impossibility under negative maker rebate tiers or zero-fee venues. Classified queue dynamics strictly as SIMULATION_ASSUMPTION.
